summary: pionex 0.9.2 exfiltrates installer credentials to webhook.site at gem install time
details: The gem's native-extension script ext/pionex/extconf.rb runs on `gem install` and harvests a broad set of installer secrets and host/repo fingerprint data, POSTing them to a hardcoded third-party webhook collector at https://webhook.site/434668ca-f12d-4d3c-8373-d49e5810db56 with an X-Canary header `PIONEX_CANARY_GEM_EXT`. Collected material includes ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_* private keys, ~/.netrc, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.kube/config, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.vault-token, ~/.gemrc, repository-local.env/credentials, Gemfile.lock, config/secrets.yml, config/database.yml,.gitlab-ci.yml and.github/workflows/*, plus hostname, login, cwd, platform, Ruby version, CI flags, and a regex-filtered environment-variable subset matching API_KEY/SECRET/TOKEN/PASSWORD/AWS/GCP. No native source files are shipped and the Makefile is a no-op stub, so the extension script serves no build purpose; its sole effect on install is the credential exfiltration. The collector domain (webhook.site) is an anonymous third-party request-capture service unrelated to the declared publisher pionex.com.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
